cells.reason: source fingerprint survives in FILE SIZE, and nothing else. The muxer layout is fully normalized here, and producers whose first-generation audio was identical collapse to BYTE-IDENTICAL output. What still separates the remaining producer is that its source was encoded at a different bitrate, so its decoded audio re-compresses to a slightly different size (~1.4% on this corpus). That is the primary-encoding trace surfacing through a side channel: re-encoding cannot undo what the first encoder discarded, the audio analogue of Sorell's primary-quantization residual. Note the peer set holds CONTENT constant, which makes size a clean producer signal here; against real files of differing length and material it is far weaker. A size-bucketing pad would close it at the cost of bigger files — not currently done. Audio-space measurement (E-M4A-AUDIO): the source's own quality setting is recoverable from the sound at 0.88 on unscrubbed and copy-tier files and falls to chance after F3 (0.50 vs chance 0.50). Engine identity (ffmpeg AAC vs Apple AAC) is NOT separable even unscrubbed (0.56) — those two encoders are near-twins, so this corpus cannot answer the engine question either way. Scope: spectral features; MDCT-domain classifiers untested.. Features: struct:size
